# Headway

> Headway Ag LLC (Stuart, Florida, USA) builds solar ear tags that hold a virtual fence for cattle, watch every animal and detect lightning, and a ranch app with no subscription for grazing plans, herd records, money and farm tax forms. Tags are in testing. Patent pending. Contact: hughheadwayag@gmail.com

## Key facts

- Company: Headway Ag LLC, Stuart, Florida, USA
- Product: Solar ear tags for virtual fencing of cattle, and a ranch app with no subscription
- Livestock: Cattle, beef and dairy
- Worn as: An ear tag, not a neck collar
- Power: Solar, charged every day on the ear
- Cue: Sound first. A mild stimulus only as the last step, with hard limits
- Also does: Guiding and splitting the herd, automatic weight records with a walk-over scale, lightning detection, theft and no movement alerts, track replay
- Records: Tagged at birth, full life history, health and genetics, read in the field by phone tap
- App: Live map, grazing planner, herd records, money and farm tax forms. No subscription
- Status: Tags in testing. Patent pending
- Contact: hughheadwayag@gmail.com

Meet the Headway ear tag.
The tag sits on one side of the ear and a small pod on the other, joined by a pin through the ear. Solar on top and sealed for life outside. It plays the tone, finds the herd and hears the weather.

## How virtual fencing for cattle works | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/virtual-fencing/

How virtual fencing for cattle works | Headway
Skip to the page
How a virtual fence works
Draw the line on a map. The tags hold it. A tone warns first.
1
Draw it
Trace a paddock, a strip or a keep-out zone on the farm map. Save it and it goes to every tag in the mob.
2
Warn it
As a cow walks toward the line her tag plays a tone. Most cattle turn around right there.
3
Hold it
Keep walking and the tone gets stronger. A mild stimulus is the last step, with hard limits. Too far out and the tag goes quiet and tells you.
Cross fence a pasture with a few clicks.
Grazing breaks, creek banks, under-used corners, water points and pivot towers can all be fenced in or fenced out from the map. Choosing where cattle graze and for how long is how you build soil health and better grass.
A virtual fence is a management tool. It is not a legal perimeter fence, and it does not replace the permanent fence along your road and boundary.
Photo: Photo by Bob Nichols, USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service. , Public domain , resized

Back fence

## Keep-out zones for cattle: creeks, yards, pivots | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/virtual-fencing/keep-out-zones.html

Keep-out zones for cattle: creeks, yards, pivots | Headway
Skip to the page
Keep-out zones
Some places inside a paddock are off limits: a creek bank, the house yard, a pivot tower, old machinery. Draw them out.
A keep-out zone works like any other line. A cow that walks toward it hears the tone and turns. You do not need clever paddock shapes to keep cattle off a creek. You draw the creek out.
Protect creek banks and let them heal.
Keep the herd off the yard and the road gate.
Fence around a pivot tower or a bog without a post.
No limit on keep-out zones. Draw as many as your place needs.
Photo: Photo by Scott Bauer, USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service. , Public domain , resized

## Virtual fencing and animal welfare | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/virtual-fencing/welfare.html

Virtual fencing and animal welfare | Headway
Skip to the page
Animal welfare comes first
Sound does the work. A mild stimulus is only ever the last step, and the tag has hard limits it cannot break.
Sound first, always
Every crossing starts with a tone, then a stronger tone. Most cattle never go further than that.
Never on the way back
An animal walking back toward the paddock is never cued. Turning back is the goal.
Not while running
A scared or running animal gets left alone.
Hard limits
A small number of stimuli per crossing and per day, with a gap between each one.
Too far out, go quiet
If an animal ends up well outside the line the tag stops cueing and tells you, so it is never stuck on the wrong side.
Unsure of position, no cue
If the tag is not sure where it is, it does nothing.
These rules are written into the tag software itself and tested every time it is built. They are not settings that can be switched off.

## How to choose a virtual fence for cattle | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/virtual-fencing/choosing.html

How to choose a virtual fence for cattle | Headway
Skip to the page
How to choose a virtual fence
Virtual fencing is a long-term choice for your operation. Here are the questions to ask any company before you buy, and how Headway answers them.
What does it cost per head per year, including data?
The Headway app has no subscription. Tag pricing will be published before the first sale.
How long does it run through a cloudy week?
Headway tags check their position less often in a long cloudy spell, but never near the line, so the fence holds.
Does it work with no cell signal?
The grazing plan is stored on every Headway tag, so planned moves happen with no signal.
Can I keep animals out of a creek or the yard inside a paddock?
Yes. Headway has keep-out zones inside each paddock.
Can I pause it while I feed?
Yes. Pause a mob's tags from the app, and turn them back on when you are done.
What happens to an animal that ends up outside the line?
The Headway tag goes quiet and tells you where the animal is, so it is never pushed away from home.
Is it worn on the neck or the ear?
Headway is an ear tag. There is no neck strap to stretch, snap or catch.
Is the app made for a computer, or only a phone?
The Headway app is made for a computer and tablet first, and works on a phone.
Does it help with the rest of the ranch?
The Headway app includes grazing plans, money and farm tax forms at no charge.
Can I talk to ranchers who use it?
Ask every company this. Headway's pilot ranches will be glad to talk once the pilot is running.
Do your homework
Ask each company to put you in touch with ranchers who use it.
Check prices in your own currency and ask what changes at renewal.
Ask what you need to buy besides the devices: base stations, towers or data plans.
Look at a real month of alerts from a ranch like yours.

## Lightning detection for cattle | Headway ear tags

URL: https://headwayfence.com/ear-tag/lightning.html

Lightning detection for cattle | Headway ear tags
Skip to the page
Lightning detection on every animal
Lightning kills cattle every year, often bunched under a lone tree or along a wire fence. Headway tags listen for it right where the herd is.
Each tag hears lightning strikes and estimates how far away they are.
The app tells you when a storm is getting closer to the herd.
One tap moves the herd off the high ground or away from the lone tree to open ground.
Strikes are logged, so you can see how often storms hit each part of the place.
A virtual fence has one more advantage here. There is no wire for lightning to run along.
Photo: USFWS Mountain Prairie , Public domain , resized

Farm tax forms, filled in as you go
Every expense you add lands on the right line of your country's farm form. At year end you send your accountant one file.
United States Schedule F (Form 1040)
Australia Business and professional items schedule, P8, with BAS
South Africa ITR12 farming income, with VAT201
Canada T2042 Statement of Farming Activities, 2025
United Kingdom SA103F Self-employment (full), tax year 2025-26 (6 Apr 2025 to 5 Apr 2026), with SA100 Tax Return
Ireland Form 11 Income Tax Return 2025 (ROS), Panel B Self-Employed Income, Extracts From Accounts lines 124-168
New Zealand IR3F Farming income (attaches to the IR3 Individual tax return), year ended 31 March 2026
Brazil Demonstrativo da Atividade Rural (ficha da DIRPF 2026, ano-calendario 2025), pessoa fisica produtor rural
Argentina Ganancias Personas Humanas, F.711 (ARCA), tax year 2025, third category farm income
Mexico Declaracion Anual de Personas Fisicas 2025 (SAT online), Actividad empresarial - Titulo IV, Cap. II, Seccion I LISR (persona fisica, actividad ganadera)
Kenya IT1 Individual Income Tax Return (resident individual, farming income section), KRA iTax, year of income 2025
Zimbabwe ITF 12C Income Tax Self Assessment Return, tax year ended 31 December 2025
Any other country A clean farm income and expense statement your accountant can move onto your form.
The app picks your country from where your ranch is. Drafts only. A tax professional in your country checks and files.

About Headway
Headway Ag LLC is a ranch technology company in Stuart, Florida. We build Headway: solar ear tags that hold a virtual fence for cattle, and an app with no subscription that runs the rest of the ranch.
Why we build it
Fence is slow and costly to build and move. Good grazing needs the herd in the right place for the right time, every time. Headway makes that a few taps instead of a few days of work.
We build on Holistic Management: people, money and land planned together. That is why the app does grazing, money and tax, not just fence lines.
How we work
Sound first, with welfare limits written into the tag.
An ear tag, not a collar.
No subscription for the app. Your data is yours.

## Virtual fencing questions answered | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/faq.html

Virtual fencing questions answered | Headway
Skip to the page
Questions about Headway
What is Headway?
Headway is a virtual fencing system for cattle made by Headway Ag LLC in Stuart, Florida. Solar ear tags hold a virtual fence line, watch every animal and detect lightning. An app with no subscription plans the grazing, moves the herd, keeps the books and fills in farm tax forms.
What is virtual fencing?
A virtual fence is a line drawn on a map in an app. Each animal wears a device that knows where it is and where the line is. As the animal walks toward the line it hears a tone, and most turn around. It lets you move cattle and cross fence pastures without building fence.
Is a virtual fence a legal perimeter fence?
No. It is a management tool for moving and holding cattle inside your place. Keep the permanent fence along roads and property lines that the law and your insurer require.
Does it hurt the cattle?
Sound does almost all the work. A mild stimulus is only ever the last step, with hard limits per crossing and per day. Tags never cue an animal walking back in or running, and go quiet if an animal ends up well outside the line.
Why an ear tag and not a collar?
Ranchers already tag ears. A tag has no neck strap to stretch, snap or catch on a fence, and it suits hairy breeds without shaving.
How is the tag powered?
A small solar panel on every tag charges it each day. The tag is sealed, so there are no batteries to swap.
What if there is no cell signal?
The grazing plan is stored on every tag, so planned moves still happen with no signal, and each tag keeps holding its line on its own.
Can it detect lightning?
Yes. Each tag hears lightning strikes, estimates how far away they are and tells you when a storm is getting closer to the herd.
Is there a subscription for the app?
No. The Headway app has no subscription model, so there is no monthly or yearly plan to sign up for. The app is in development, and the full terms will be in the Headway Software License at launch. Tags are sold separately.
Which countries does the tax tool cover?
The United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, Brazil, Argentina, Mexico, Kenya and Zimbabwe, plus a plain income and expense pack for anywhere else. Your accountant checks and files.
Which animals does Headway work with?
Headway is being built for beef and dairy cattle first.
Can Headway guide, split or move the herd?
Yes. You can walk a mob down a moving virtual lane to new ground, or split calves, steers or cows due to calve into their own mob with its own line, from the app.
Does the tag weigh cattle?
No. The tag does not weigh anything. It records weights automatically with a walk-over scale, which you buy separately and set up at the water point. On weigh days the herd is guided to water through the scale lane, on a schedule you pick. The scale weighs each animal, the tag tells it who is on it, and the weight is saved to that animal's record with no typing.
Can a vet see an animal's record in the field?
Yes. Hold a phone to the tag and the record opens. The tag carries its ID and key health notes, so the basics show even with no signal.
Does Headway keep health and genetics records?
Yes. Each animal can be tagged at birth and keeps its whole history: birth and weaning weights, dam and sire, breed and genetic values from your breed association, vaccines, treatments with withdrawal dates, pregnancy checks, weights and moves.
When can I buy tags?
Tags are in testing now. Tell us about your ranch on the pilot page to be on the list.
How do I contact Headway?
Email hughheadwayag@gmail.com. Headway Ag LLC is based in Stuart, Florida.
Want Headway on your place?
Tell us what makes your ranch different: the herd, the ground, the weather.
Join the pilot Contact us

## Privacy and cookie choice on headwayfence.com

URL: https://headwayfence.com/privacy.html

Privacy and cookie choice on headwayfence.com
Skip to the page
Privacy and cookie choice
This page says exactly what headwayfence.com counts, what it stores in your browser, and how to change your mind.
What this site counts
The site counts page views: a number for each page and a number for each day. The counter sets no cookies and keeps no names, email addresses, payment details or location data. There is no account and no login, so nothing about you is asked for.
The counts are shown as totals only. A total cannot tell anyone who you are, and nothing here follows you around the web or shows you advertising. This site runs no ads.
What the Accept button adds
If you press Accept in the banner, one small flag is saved in this browser, on this device only. It records that you accepted and the date of a first visit that day, so repeat visitors are counted once per day. The flag has no name or account number attached. It is not a cookie and it is not sent to any advertiser.
How to opt out
Press Essential only in the banner and no flag is saved. Page views are still counted, because that total holds no personal data. If you pressed Accept and changed your mind, clear this site's data in your browser settings and the banner will ask again.
What is never collected
No name, address, phone number, password or card number. Email only reaches us when you choose to send it. No advertising trackers and no social media widgets.
Questions about this page
Headway Ag LLC runs this site from Stuart, Florida. Write to hughheadwayag@gmail.com if anything here is unclear.

## Guide, split and move cattle with virtual fencing | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/virtual-fencing/herding.html

Guide, split and move cattle with virtual fencing | Headway
Skip to the page
Guide, split and move the herd
The virtual line can move. That means you can walk a mob to new ground, hold it in a lane, or split it, all from the app.
Guide a mob
Pick a mob and where it should go. The app draws a lane from where they are to the new paddock, and the line walks them along it a little at a time. You watch them go on the map.
Split a mob
Pull the calves off the cows, the heavy steers off the light ones, or the cows due to calve into their own mob. Each new mob gets its own line on every tag.
Move on a schedule
Put moves in the grazing plan and they happen on time, every time, with or without signal.
Back into the pens
Bring a mob up the lane to the yard for working, then pause their tags while they are in.
Photo: WBRA Jen , CC BY-SA 4.0 , resized
The app is in development. Screens show demo data.

## Automatic cattle weight records | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/ear-tag/weighing.html

Automatic cattle weight records | Headway
Skip to the page
Automatic weight records
The tag does not weigh the animal. It works with a walk-over scale so every weight is recorded to the right animal on its own, without running the herd through the chute.
How it works
Set up a walk-over scale in the lane to water. The scale is bought separately.
Pick how often: every 3, 7, 14 or 30 days.
On weigh days the herd is guided to water through the scale lane.
The scale weighs each animal as it walks over. The tag says who it is, and the weight is saved to the animal record with no typing.
Every Headway tag carries a standard livestock EID chip, so scales and readers that read EID tags already know who is on the scale.
Photo: USDA NRCS Texas , Public domain , resized
Daily gain
Weight gain per day for each animal, each mob and the whole herd.
Who is falling behind
An animal that stops gaining goes to the top of your list. That is often the first sign of trouble.
Sell on time
See which steers are at target weight this week, without guessing.

## Tap a tag: cattle records in the field | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/ear-tag/tap-a-tag.html

Tap a tag: cattle records in the field | Headway
Skip to the page
Tap a tag for the record
Hold a phone to the ear tag and that animal's record opens. Made for the vet in the pen and the rancher in the paddock.
Phone tap: the tag can be read by a phone held close to it.
No signal needed for the basics: the tag carries its ID and key health notes, such as the last treatment and the withdrawal date.
Standard EID too: chute readers and scales that read livestock EID tags can read it.
Add a treatment right there, and it is saved to the record.
Photo: BLM Oregon & Washington , Public domain , resized

## Cattle health, genetics and lifetime records | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/software/records.html

Cattle health, genetics and lifetime records | Headway
Skip to the page
Health, genetics and lifetime records
Tag a calf the day it is born and keep its whole story in one place, from birth weight to sale.
Tagged at birth
Record the calving and the calf gets its record that day: born, dam, sire, birth weight.
Genetics
Dam, sire, breed and genetic values from your breed association records, on every animal.
Health log
Vaccines and treatments, with the withdrawal date worked out for you.
Weights
Birth, weaning and every scale weight since, with daily gain.
Behaviour
Time spent grazing, resting and walking, and alerts when it changes.
Moves
Every paddock it has been in and when, from the tags.
Ready for the vet and the buyer
Pull up the full history in the field with a phone tap, or export it for a buyer, a vet or a breed registry.
Your records are yours. Export everything any time.

## Ranch and virtual fencing words explained | Headway

URL: https://headwayfence.com/glossary.html

Ranch and virtual fencing words explained | Headway
Skip to the page
Ranch and virtual fence words
Plain meanings for the words used on this site and in the Headway app.
Virtual fence A boundary drawn on a map in an app and held by a device on each animal, using sound first instead of wire and posts. Virtual fencing Managing where livestock graze with virtual fences instead of physical fence, so lines can be drawn and moved from an app. Break A smaller strip or section of a paddock that a mob grazes for a short time before moving to the next one. Strip grazing Giving the herd a fresh break of grass every day or two, with a back fence so grazed ground can rest. Mob A group of animals managed together, such as cows and calves or a group of steers. Paddock A fenced or virtually fenced area of pasture. Keep-out zone An area inside a paddock that animals are kept out of, such as a creek bank, the house yard or a pivot tower. Rest period The number of days since a paddock was last grazed. Good rest lets grass regrow and roots stay deep. Stocking rate How many animals the land carries, often measured in animal units per acre or hectare. Animal unit A standard measure of grazing demand, roughly one 1,000 lb cow with or without a calf. Grazing days How many days a break or paddock can feed a mob before it should move. Holistic Management A way of planning that looks at people, money and land together and tests every decision against what you want. EID tag A livestock ID tag with a tiny radio chip that scales and chute readers can read, using the ISO 11784 and 11785 standards. Walk-over scale A scale set in a lane, often on the way to water, that weighs each animal as it walks across. Average daily gain How much weight an animal puts on per day between two weighings. Withdrawal period The number of days after a treatment before an animal can be sold for meat or its milk used. EPD Expected progeny difference: a breed association estimate of how an animal's calves will compare on a trait such as birth weight. Dam and sire An animal's mother and father. NFC Near field communication: a short range radio that lets a phone read a tag held close to it. Tone The sound a Headway tag plays as an animal walks toward a virtual fence line. Most cattle turn back on the tone. Mild stimulus The last step in a virtual fence cue, used only after the tones, with hard limits per crossing and per day.
